rows.author: D039
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING DUE COMPENSATION TO ELEMENTARY SCHOOL TEACHERS HANDLING `MULTI-GRADE CLASSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: Comparatively, a school teacher who handles a multi-grade class encounters greater difficulty and responsibilitie s than a school teacher who handles a single-grade class, in terms of consolidating and integrating multi-level instructions/ma terials in the different learning areas, lesson plans/exercises and examinations within one class session. Despite the differences in the scope of and degree of responsibilitie s, however, at present, a school teacher handling a multi-grade classreceives the standard monthly remuneration given to all teachers who do not engage in multi-grade instructions. This bill thereby endeavors to resolve such disparity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-10-08

rows.author: D039
rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING THE COMPETITIVENESS AND ESTABLISHING THE SELF-RELIANCE OF THE NATIONAL PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "National Pharmaceutical Industries Omnibus Act of 1999". Rationale:  A profile of the Philippine pharmaceutical industry reveals that it is oligopolistic in structure, dominated by foreign corporation or multinational companies (MNC's) cornering almost ninety percent (90%) of the total market for pharmaceuticals , mostly composed of branded leading products. Distribution channels for drugs and medicines are likewise composed of foreign multinational firms distributing the products of the manufacturers. Filipino-owned and -controlled companies manufacturing and distributing generic drugs and medicines comprise only 12% to 15% of the total market.  This bill, therefore, seeks to address those concerns: >1. Establishment of an effective drugg regulatory system; 2. Provision of safe, affordable and accessible drugs and medicines; and 3. Initiation of ways and means to increase the global competitiveness and self-reliance of the local pharmaceutical industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-10-08

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE TARIFF RATES ON VARIOUS TARIFF HEADINGS UNDER SECTION 104 OF THE TARIFF AND CUSTOMS CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The situation of the Philippine business and local industry sector continued to deteriorate since the Asian crisis of 1997.  It is of common knowledge that the manufacturing sector has suffered an enormous decline in productivity, resulting in numerous cases of slowdown, temporary work stoppage, and in many instances, total closure of facilities. It is in this context that this bill is being proposed so as to respond significantly to the clamor for government support from the domestic industries severely affected by the unhealthy business climate.  This is achieved by maintaining, the current tariff rates on certain articles that are being manufactured by the local industries up to year 2002 and reducing to zero rate all tariffss currently at three (3%) which are imposed on local industries' raw materials and inputs not locally manufactured.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The period for filing free patent was terminated last December 31, 2000, as provided for in RA 6940. Consequently, there are some individuals with application for free patent who were unable to avail of the gratuitous grant of the state although their claims are legitimate as the administrative confirmation of title was discontinued. >Free patent ishe most affordable means by which a legitimate claimant can acquire a title over the land lawfully occupied. This is different from the other modes of granting land titles which require judicial proceedings. In such procedure, an individual has to undergo tedious and lengthy court proceedings aside from the litigation expenses that usually accompany this mode of issuing land titles.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Given the recent turn of events and the current alarm over terrorist acts, there is a need to establish a national identification system. Moreover, it provides for an effective method of solving the perennial problem of red tape in government bureaucracy. It facilitates in the acquisition of records for a short period of time. Criminal activities are easily monitored and the perpetrators apprehended and prosecuted without delay. Public documents can now be accessed immediately for itshall contain data such as taxpayer's identification number, NBI records, driver's license, voter's identification and the like.

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING THE RETIREMENT AGE FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS FROM SIXTY (60) TO FIFTY-FIVE (55) YEARS OLD AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Any public teacher, upon reaching the age of fifty five (55) years but not beyond the compulsory retirement age of sixty (60) years, and has served at least twenty (20) years as a public school teacher, may retire and shall immediately be entitled to all the retirement benefits provided for under the existing laws. >Our public school teachers deserve to enjoy the fruits of their labors. Lowering their compulsory retirement age to 55 years will ensure that our teachers will have the opportunityto fully utilize their benefits and enjoy their life free from the pressures of their job. Thus, for humanitarian reasons, the passage of this bill is earnestly requested.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-10-08

rows.abstract: Rationale: The latest trend in telecommunicati ons has provided much convenience for everyone. Business transactions have definitely been made more efficient and effective since the advent of the mobile cellular phone technology. However, access tothe technology through the purchase and use of Prepaid Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) Packs has been too easy and uncontrolled. Unscrupulous individuals have taken advantage of this unregistered sale of SIM packs to hide themselves behind an untraceable number to mask the pursuit of their illegal or criminal activities to the deteriment of many Filipinos. > The proposed bill aims to address the inability of law engorcement agencies to track down criminals or individuals using mobile phones astools in the commission of a crime or in many cases, to harass, to communicate threats, to send ransom demands or simply, to make an obscene phone call or send an obscene text message.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-10-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL PALM OIL DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish a NATIONAL PALM OIL DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY. The concept and the objective is to assist both the businessmen and farmers engage in the business of palm oil to expand its operations by providing them sufficient informationand technology. It shall likewise provide a one-stop shop which shall facilitate the processing and documentation of all paper requirements necessary for the credit facilities. From the record, it is clear that the palm oil industry has been considered as one of the major sources of national income of the government in the form of business taxes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-10-09

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-08-27, transmitted to on 2002-09-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-09-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING THE COLLECTIONS FROM THE TRAVEL TAX TO THE PHILIPPINE TOURISM AUTHORITY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The Travel Tax was originally envisioned and promulgated for the purpose of promoting travel and tourism, development of tourist attractions and to provide financial assistance to private tourism enterprises. However, due to the enormous laws passedwhich provided for the allocation of funds mainly from Travel Tax collections, the source of funding of the Philippine Tourism Authority was greatly diminished, thus, resulting to the delayed delivery of basic support services to the tourism industry. Moreover, tourism marketing and promotional activities were very much hampered due to the lack of funding from the Philippine Tourism Authority. This bill is a curative legislation. It seeks to remedy a malady brought about by the dearth of fundsin the coffers of the government.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04918

rows.author: D085
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09208) enacted on 2003-05-26
rows.title_full: AN ACT CRIMINALIZING TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS SPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ITS VIOLATIONS, AND INSTITUTING POLICIES TO COMBAT TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS SPECIALLY WOMEN AND MINORS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL AND APPROPRIATE SOCIO-ECONOMIC ALTERNATIVES, AND ESTABLISHING THE NECESSARY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS FOR ITS PREVENTION, AND PROTECTION AND SUPPORT OF TRAFFICKED PERSONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: An immediate concern is the fact that there is no Philippine law that clearly defines trafficking as a crime.  This bill addresses this concern by declaring trafficking as a crime and imposing appropriate penalties on traffickers. This bill also aims to provide opportunities for the coordination of efforts by government agencies, NGOs and people's organizations toward a more effective approach at combating trafficking in persons specially women and minors. >This bill includes provisions that provide guidelines on the: (1) Development of local and appropriate economic and social alternatives to address poverty in urban and rural poor communities. (2) Role of local government units, people's organizations and NGOs at the grassroots level incombating trafficking persons in urban and rural poor communities.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04432

rows.abstract: There shall be established a Philippine citizenship identification (ID) system in the Philippines to be administered by the Bureau of Immigration, which is hereby mandated to determine, validate and issue certificates of citizenship to all Filipinocitizens in accordance with existing laws. rows.abstract: Natural-born citizens of the Philippines who have been naturalized citizens in other countries shall enjoy the rights and privileges enjoyed by Filipino citizens without renouncing their citizenship in their adoptive countries. Some of the RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES referred to are:  (1) To vote and run for public office, except as President and Vice President; (2) To seek employment; (3) To exploit the country's natural resources; (4) To operate public utilities, rural banks; (5) To engage in retail trade, etc.

rows.author: D078
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPUTERIZED VOTER'S IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM
rows.abstract: It is hereby declared a state policy to establish a voter's identification system as a means to ensure the integrity of the electoral process. Under this system, every registered voter shall, upon registration, furnish and make available his personal data to the Commission on Elections. >The voter's identification system shall be implemented by providing each bonafide years voter at least eighteen years old, a voter's identification card which shall contain the following personal data: (a) voter's name; (b) voter's sex; (c) voter's place of birth; (d) names of voter's parents; (e) voter's place of residence; (f) voter's photograph; (g) voter's signature; (h) voter's right-thumb mark; (i) voter's identification number.  >Each voter's identiification card shall also bear the signature of the Chairman of the Commission on Elections. The voter's indentification number shall be permanent and shall be entered in the central computerized database of the Commission on Elections.

rows.abstract: This bill contains AMENDATORY provision to RA No. 6425, the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972, such as: 1. Provision for the increase in Board Membership by involving a wider spectrum of the government strata and non-government participation in the policy-making arena; 2. Provision for a single definition of Dangerous Drugs, which covers both prohibited and regulated drugs. 3. Provision for a definition of Dangerous Drugs Preparations, which includes Precursors and Essential Chemicals, as well as control mechanisms for the licit trade of such, and penalties for violation thereof; 4. rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 31 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6770, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE OMBUDSMAN ACT OF 1989', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Section 31 of Republic Act No. 6770 is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 31. Designation of Investigators and Prosecutors. The Ombudsman may utilize the personnel of his office and/or designate any fiscal, state, prosecutor, or lawyer inthe government service to act as special investigator or prosecutor to assist in the investigation and prosecution of certain cases. THE OMBUDSMAN MAY ALSO DEPUTIZE LAWYERS IN PRIVATE PRACTICE, FREE OF CHARGE, TO PROSECUTE OR ASSIST IN THE PROSECUTION OF CERTAIN CASES. Those designated or deputized to assist him as herein provided shall be under his supervision and control. >It is urgent and imperative that if we are to win the war against corruption and erring public officials, the prosecutoriaal arm of the State - the Ombudsman - be reinforced by authorizing the deputization of private lawyers as prosecutors under the direct supervision and control of the Ombudsman.

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ENTRY, SALE, PROCESSING, FIELD TESTING AND RELEASE OF CROPS AND FOOD PRODUCTS CONTAINING GENETICALLY ENGINEERED ORGANISMS (GEO) INTO AND WITHIN THE COUNTRY AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "GEO-Free Food and Agriculture Act of 2001." This bill aims to keep the country's food and agriculture free from genetically engineered organisms at this time when there are still unresolved questions as to its possible adverse effects on human health and the environment. The filing of this bill does not mean that the bill's authors are against the use of science and technology in food and agriculture. On the contrary, the proponents of this bill firmly believe in using science to serve the people and society.  But they are strongly opposed to the use of science that will benefit only a few and worse, hurt people and damage the environment.

rows.abstract: Section 5 of PD 1275 is hereby amended to read as follows: "Section 5. Compensation. THE SECRETARY OF JUSTICE IS HEREBY AUTHORIZED TO PREPARE A COMPENSATION STRUCTURE FOR THE NATIONAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (NAPROSS) WHICH SHALL BE BASED ON A COMPREHENSIVE JOB ANALYSIS AND AUDIT OF ACTUAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIE S AND SHALL BE COMPARABLE WITH THE PREVAILING COMPENSATION PLAN IN THE PRACTICE OF THE LEGAL PROFESSION IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR. rows.author: C109
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION SYSTEM COUNCIL, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to formalize the different identification systems into one uniform system for the entire country which shall be known as the National Identification System (NIS). It will have various subsystems such as the School Identification System (SIS), Professional Identification System (PIS), Voter's Identification System (VIS), Drivers' Identification System (DIS), Social Security System Identification System (SSSIS), Government Service Insurance System Identification System (GSISIS), and the Bureau of Internal REvenue Identification System (BIRIS).  >A uniform system is practical and economical to implement. It can properly and efficiently identify persons seeking basic services and social security and reduce if not eradicate ffraudulent transactions and misrepresentati ons.  To achieve the realization of such system, a concerted and collaborative effort among the various sectors and government agencies are enjoined.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-10-15

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING FOR A PERIOD OF FIVE (5) YEARS ENDING ON DECEMBER 31, 2005 THE FILING OF APPLICATIONS FOR FREE PATENT AND JUDICIAL CONFIRMATION OF IMPERFECT TITLE TO ALIENABLE AND DISPOSABLE LANDS OF THE PUBLIC DOMAIN UNDER CHAPTERS VII AND VIII OFTHE PUBLIC LAND ACT (CA 141, AS AMENDED)
rows.abstract: In order to attain social justice in all phases of national development, especially in agriculture, it is necessary that farmers and settlers be given all the changes to acquire clean and clear titles to the lands they have cultivated and settled in. Thus, they can continue their stewardship of such lands with confidence, assured that whatever they put into these lands - time, money and efforts - shall redound to their benefits. Such confidence may, in turn, make them more resourceful and moreindustrious. One way to give them confidence is to extend the period for filing application for free patent and judicial confirmation of imperfect title to alienable and disposable lands of the public domain to another five years ending on December 331, 2005.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04628
